3. 3. Governance and Responsibilities
The governance framework for RWA treatment is overseen by the bank’s Board of Directors, which retains ultimate
responsibility for ensuring compliance with Basel IV and this policy. The Board delegates operational responsibility to the Group
Chief Risk Officer (CRO), who is accountable for the implementation, monitoring, and enforcement of the RWA treatment
methodologies. The CRO is supported by the Risk Management Committee (RMC), which provides strategic oversight and
approves any material changes to the policy.
The Credit Risk Department (CRD) is responsible for the day-to-day application of the RWA treatment policy. This includes
developing and maintaining the methodologies, tools, and systems used for RWA calculations. The CRD is also tasked with
conducting periodic validations of the RWA models to ensure their accuracy and reliability. Any discrepancies or issues
identified during these validations must be escalated to the RMC for resolution.
Business units, such as Corporate Banking, Retail Banking, and Treasury, are responsible for ensuring that their credit
exposures are classified and reported in accordance with the RWA treatment policy. Each business unit must designate a
Credit Risk Officer (CRO) who acts as the primary point of contact for RWA-related queries and ensures compliance with the
policy within their respective areas. These officers are required to undergo annual training on RWA treatment methodologies
and regulatory updates.
The Internal Audit function is responsible for conducting independent reviews of the bank’s RWA treatment processes at least
once every two years. The audit scope includes assessing the effectiveness of controls, the accuracy of RWA calculations, and
the adherence to policy requirements. Findings from these audits are reported to the Audit Committee of the Board, which
ensures that any identified deficiencies are addressed promptly.

not aligned with the true economic risk of the exposure. For example, a waiver may be requested for a collateralized exposure
where the collateral’s value significantly exceeds the exposure amount, making the standard risk weight overly conservative.
Waivers must be supported by a robust analysis, including an independent valuation of the collateral and a comparison of the
proposed RWA treatment against alternative approaches.
All exceptions and waivers must be approved by the appropriate authority, based on the size and risk of the exposure.
Exceptions for exposures up to USD 10 million may be approved by the Business Unit Head, while exceptions for exposures
between USD 10 million and USD 50 million require approval from the relevant Regional Risk Committee (RRC). Exceptions for
exposures exceeding USD 50 million, or those involving novel or complex structures, must be approved by the Group Risk
Management Committee (RMC).
The policy requires that all exceptions and waivers be documented in the bank’s central repository, with a clear audit trail of the
approval process. Exceptions and waivers are subject to periodic review, typically on an annual basis, to ensure that they

The policy also mandates that the bank disclose its RWA treatment methodologies and key metrics in its annual financial

use of internal models (where applicable), and the impact of RWA on the bank’s capital adequacy. The disclosures are
reviewed by the bank’s Legal and Compliance functions to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and industry best
practices.
Internal reporting is supplemented by ad-hoc reports, which are produced in response to specific requests from senior
management, the RMC, or regulatory authorities. These reports may focus on specific aspects of the bank’s RWA treatment

with the involvement of the Credit Risk Department (CRD), the Risk Management Committee (RMC), and other relevant
stakeholders. The review process includes an assessment of the policy’s effectiveness in managing RWA, as well as an

 A.2 Capital Floors
REG-Basel-IV §A.2 · Effective 2026-09-10

1. 1. Purpose
The purpose of this Capital Floors Policy (the 'Policy') is to establish a robust framework for the implementation, monitoring, and
enforcement of capital floor requirements in accordance with the Basel IV regulatory standards. This Policy ensures that the
Bank maintains a minimum level of capital that mitigates risks arising from underestimation or miscalculation of risk-weighted
assets (RWAs) under internal models. By setting a floor, the Bank guarantees that its capital adequacy ratio does not fall below
a specified threshold, thereby safeguarding financial stability and regulatory compliance.
This Policy is designed to address the potential discrepancies between the Bank’s internal risk assessments and the
standardized approaches prescribed by regulatory authorities. It ensures that the Bank’s capital planning and risk management
practices are aligned with the principles of prudence, transparency, and accountability. The Policy also serves as a critical
control mechanism to prevent excessive leverage and to maintain public trust in the Bank’s financial resilience.
The Capital Floors Policy is a synthetic demonstration document created for illustrative purposes. It reflects industry best
practices and regulatory expectations but does not represent the actual policies, procedures, or practices of any real financial
institution. All thresholds, roles, and processes described herein are fictional and intended solely for training, testing, or
educational use.
This Policy applies universally across all business units, subsidiaries, and jurisdictions in which the Bank operates. It is binding
on all employees, contractors, and third parties acting on behalf of the Bank. Compliance with this Policy is mandatory, and any
deviations must be justified, documented, and approved through the established governance framework.
The Policy is reviewed annually or more frequently if there are significant changes in regulatory requirements, the Bank’s risk
profile, or its operational environment. The review process ensures that the Policy remains relevant, effective, and aligned with
the Bank’s strategic objectives and regulatory obligations.

REG-Basel-IV §A.2 | Synthetic policy data
Page 2

2. 2. Scope
This Policy applies to all material risk exposures of the Bank, including but not limited to credit risk, market risk, operational risk,
and counterparty credit risk. It covers all business lines, legal entities, and geographical regions where the Bank conducts its
operations. The scope includes all internal models used for calculating RWAs, as well as the standardized approaches for
comparison and validation purposes.
The Capital Floors Policy is particularly relevant to the Bank’s Internal Ratings-Based (IRB) approaches for credit risk,
Advanced Measurement Approaches (AMA) for operational risk, and internal models for market risk. For each of these areas,
the Policy establishes a floor based on a percentage of the RWAs calculated using the standardized approach. The floor is set
at 72.5% of the standardized RWAs, as per Basel IV requirements, to ensure consistency and comparability.
Exposures that are not material in terms of their contribution to the Bank’s overall risk profile may be excluded from the scope of
this Policy, provided that such exclusions are justified, documented, and approved by the Risk Management Committee (RMC).
The materiality threshold for exclusion is defined as any exposure that constitutes less than 1% of the Bank’s total RWAs.
Exclusions must be reviewed annually to ensure they remain appropriate.
The Policy also applies to all new products, services, and business activities introduced by the Bank. Prior to launch, these
must undergo a capital floor assessment to ensure compliance with the Policy’s requirements. The assessment must be
conducted by the Risk Management Department (RMD) in collaboration with the relevant business unit and submitted to the
RMC for approval.
For jurisdictions where local regulations impose additional or different capital floor requirements, the Bank will comply with the
stricter of the two standards. The RMD is responsible for monitoring regulatory developments and ensuring that the Policy is
updated to reflect any changes in local or international requirements.

REG-Basel-IV §A.2 | Synthetic policy data

3. 3. Governance
The governance framework for this Policy is designed to ensure clear accountability, transparency, and effective oversight. The
Board of Directors (the 'Board') retains ultimate responsibility for the approval and periodic review of the Policy. The Board
delegates the implementation and day-to-day management of the Policy to the RMC, which is chaired by the Chief Risk Officer
(CRO).
The RMC is responsible for ensuring that the Policy is implemented consistently across the Bank and that all business units
adhere to its requirements. The RMC meets quarterly to review the effectiveness of the Policy, assess compliance with capital
floor requirements, and address any emerging risks or issues. Minutes of these meetings, including action items and decisions,
are documented and made available to the Board and relevant regulators upon request.
The RMD, under the leadership of the CRO, is tasked with the operational implementation of the Policy. This includes
developing procedures, tools, and methodologies for calculating and monitoring capital floors, as well as providing training and
guidance to business units. The RMD is also responsible for conducting independent reviews and audits to verify compliance
with the Policy.
Business unit heads are accountable for ensuring that their respective areas comply with the Policy. They must designate a
Capital Floor Coordinator within their unit to serve as the primary point of contact for the RMD. Coordinators are responsible for
providing accurate and timely data, addressing any non-compliance issues, and escalating material risks or breaches to the
RMC.
The Internal Audit Department (IAD) conducts an annual audit of the Policy’s effectiveness and the Bank’s compliance with its
requirements. The audit includes a review of the capital floor calculations, the accuracy of RWAs, and the adequacy of controls
and escalation procedures. Findings and recommendations from the audit are presented to the RMC and the Board for action.

REG-Basel-IV §A.2 | Synthetic policy data
Page 4

4. 4. Underwriting Criteria
The underwriting criteria outlined in this section are designed to ensure that all credit exposures subject to the Capital Floors
Policy are originated and managed in a manner consistent with the Bank’s risk appetite and regulatory requirements. These
criteria apply to all new and renewed exposures, including loans, derivatives, and other credit facilities.
For credit exposures assessed under the IRB approach, the Bank must ensure that the estimated Probability of Default (PD),
Loss Given Default (LGD), and Exposure at Default (EAD) parameters are conservative and supported by robust historical data
and forward-looking analysis. The PD, LGD, and EAD estimates must be validated annually by an independent party, such as
the Model Validation Team (MVT), to ensure their accuracy and reliability.
The Bank’s underwriting process must incorporate a capital floor assessment for all material exposures. This assessment
involves comparing the RWAs calculated under the IRB approach with those calculated under the standardized approach. If the
IRB RWAs are less than 72.5% of the standardized RWAs, the difference must be justified and documented. Justifications must
be based on objective evidence, such as the quality of the underlying data, the robustness of the model, or the specific risk
characteristics of the exposure.
For exposures where the capital floor is breached, the underwriting process must include an escalation to the RMC for
approval. The escalation must include a detailed analysis of the reasons for the breach, the potential risks, and the proposed
mitigation measures. The RMC may approve the exposure if it is satisfied that the risks are adequately managed and that the
breach does not pose a material threat to the Bank’s capital adequacy.
The underwriting criteria also require that all credit exposures be subject to ongoing monitoring and review. This includes
regular updates to the PD, LGD, and EAD parameters, as well as periodic reassessments of the capital floor compliance. Any
material changes in the risk profile of an exposure must be reported to the RMD and, if necessary, escalated to the RMC.

REG-Basel-IV §A.2 | Synthetic policy data
Page 5

5. 5. Quantitative Limits
The Capital Floors Policy establishes quantitative limits to ensure that the Bank’s capital adequacy ratio remains above the
minimum regulatory requirements. The primary limit is the capital floor, which is set at 72.5% of the RWAs calculated using the
standardized approach. This means that the RWAs calculated under the Bank’s internal models must not be less than 72.5% of
the RWAs calculated under the standardized approach for the same exposures.
In addition to the capital floor, the Policy introduces a series of internal triggers and thresholds to monitor and manage capital
adequacy. The first trigger is activated when the Bank’s Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio falls below 10.5%. At this
point, the RMD must conduct a detailed review of the Bank’s capital position and submit a report to the RMC within 10 business
days, outlining the causes of the decline and the proposed corrective actions.
A second trigger is activated when the CET1 capital ratio falls below 9.5%. In this case, the RMC must convene an emergency
meeting within 5 business days to assess the situation and develop a capital restoration plan. The plan must include specific
measures to improve the capital ratio, such as reducing risk-weighted assets, raising additional capital, or divesting non-core
assets. The plan must be approved by the Board and submitted to the relevant regulators within 15 business days.
The Policy also establishes a maximum leverage ratio of 5%, calculated as the ratio of the Bank’s Tier 1 capital to its total
exposure measure. The total exposure measure includes both on-balance sheet and off-balance sheet exposures. If the
leverage ratio exceeds 5%, the Bank must immediately notify the RMC and implement measures to reduce the ratio to within
the limit.
For trading book exposures, the Policy sets a limit on the Value-at-Risk (VaR) capital charge. The VaR capital charge must not
exceed 3 times the average VaR capital charge over the previous 60 business days. If this limit is breached, the Bank must
conduct a review of its trading activities and risk management practices and report the findings to the RMC.

REG-Basel-IV §A.2 | Synthetic policy data
Page 6

6. 6. Approvals
The approvals process under this Policy is designed to ensure that all material decisions related to capital floors are subject to
appropriate oversight and accountability. Approvals are required for the initial implementation of the Policy, any subsequent
amendments, and all exceptions or breaches of the Policy’s requirements.
Amendments to the Policy must be approved by the RMC and the Board. The process begins with a proposal from the RMD,
which is reviewed by the RMC. If the RMC approves the proposal, it is submitted to the Board for final approval. Amendments
are typically reviewed annually, but ad-hoc reviews may be conducted if there are significant changes in regulatory
requirements or the Bank’s risk profile.
Exceptions to the Policy’s requirements, such as exclusions from the scope or justifications for capital floor breaches, must be
approved by the RMC. Requests for exceptions must be submitted by the relevant business unit to the RMD, which conducts an
initial review and provides a recommendation to the RMC. The RMC considers the request at its next scheduled meeting or, if
urgent, at an ad-hoc meeting. Approvals for exceptions are valid for a maximum of 12 months, after which they must be
reviewed and reapproved.
Breaches of the capital floor or other quantitative limits must be reported to the RMC within 24 hours of identification. The RMC
must then determine whether the breach is material and, if so, escalate it to the Board. Material breaches are those that exceed
5% of the Bank’s total RWAs or result in a CET1 capital ratio below 9.5%. The RMC or Board, as applicable, must approve a
remediation plan to address the breach within 10 business days.
The Policy also requires approvals for the introduction of new internal models or significant changes to existing models. These
must be approved by the MVT, the RMC, and, in some cases, the relevant regulators. The approval process includes a
thorough validation of the model’s assumptions, methodologies, and performance, as well as an assessment of its impact on
the Bank’s capital floors.

REG-Basel-IV §A.2 | Synthetic policy data
Page 7

7. 7. Monitoring
The monitoring framework under this Policy is designed to ensure continuous compliance with capital floor requirements and to
provide early warning of potential breaches or risks. Monitoring is conducted at multiple levels, including business units, the
RMD, and the RMC, to ensure comprehensive coverage and timely escalation.
Business units are responsible for monitoring their own exposures and capital floor compliance on a daily basis. This includes
tracking RWAs calculated under both internal models and the standardized approach, as well as monitoring the capital floor
ratio for each material exposure. Business units must report any breaches or potential breaches to the RMD within 24 hours of
identification.
The RMD conducts independent monitoring of the Bank’s overall capital floor compliance on a weekly basis. This includes
aggregating data from all business units, validating the accuracy of RWAs, and assessing the Bank’s compliance with the

72.5% capital floor requirement. The RMD also monitors the Bank’s CET1 capital ratio, leverage ratio, and other quantitative
limits established under the Policy. Any breaches or trends that could lead to breaches are reported to the RMC.
The RMC reviews the Bank’s capital floor compliance on a monthly basis. This review includes an assessment of the Bank’s
overall capital position, the effectiveness of the monitoring framework, and the status of any remediation plans for breaches or
exceptions. The RMC also reviews the results of the internal audits and independent validations conducted by the IAD and the
MVT.
In addition to regular monitoring, the Policy requires the conduct of stress tests and scenario analyses on a semi-annual basis.
These tests assess the impact of adverse economic conditions, market shocks, or operational failures on the Bank’s capital
floors and overall capital adequacy. The results of the stress tests are reported to the RMC and the Board and are used to
inform the Bank’s capital planning and risk management strategies.
The Bank’s monitoring framework is supported by a suite of automated tools and systems that provide real-time data on RWAs,
capital ratios, and other key metrics. These tools are subject to regular validation and testing to ensure their accuracy and
reliability. The RMD is responsible for maintaining and updating these tools as necessary.

REG-Basel-IV §A.2 | Synthetic policy data
Page 8

8. 8. Exceptions
The Policy recognizes that there may be circumstances where strict adherence to the capital floor requirements is not feasible
or appropriate. In such cases, exceptions may be granted, provided that they are justified, documented, and approved through
the established governance framework. Exceptions are intended to be rare and are subject to strict controls and monitoring.
Exceptions may be requested for individual exposures, portfolios, or business units. Common reasons for exceptions include
the unavailability of reliable data for the standardized approach, the unique risk characteristics of an exposure that are not
captured by the internal models, or the temporary nature of a breach due to market conditions. However, exceptions cannot be
granted for systemic or persistent breaches of the capital floor.
Requests for exceptions must be submitted to the RMD using the standardized Exception Request Form. The form requires a
detailed justification for the exception, including the specific circumstances that warrant it, the potential risks, and the proposed
mitigation measures. The request must also include an assessment of the impact of the exception on the Bank’s capital
adequacy and a plan for monitoring and reviewing the exception.
The RMD reviews the request and provides a recommendation to the RMC. The RMC considers the request at its next
scheduled meeting or, if urgent, at an ad-hoc meeting. The RMC’s decision is based on the merits of the request, the potential
risks to the Bank, and the adequacy of the proposed mitigation measures. If approved, the exception is documented in the
Exception Register, which is maintained by the RMD and reviewed by the RMC on a quarterly basis.
Exceptions are valid for a maximum of 12 months, after which they must be reviewed and reapproved. The RMD is responsible
for monitoring the status of all exceptions and ensuring that they remain justified and appropriate. If the circumstances that
warranted the exception change, the RMD must reassess the exception and, if necessary, recommend its revocation to the
RMC.
All exceptions must be reported to the relevant regulators as part of the Bank’s regular regulatory reporting. The report must
include the number of exceptions, their justification, and the status of any remediation plans. The Bank must also be prepared
to provide additional information or explanations to the regulators upon request.

9. 9. Reporting
The reporting framework under this Policy is designed to provide timely, accurate, and comprehensive information on the
Bank’s capital floor compliance to senior management, the Board, and relevant regulators. Reporting is conducted at multiple
levels and frequencies to ensure that all stakeholders are informed and that issues are escalated promptly.
Business units are required to submit weekly reports to the RMD on their capital floor compliance. These reports must include
the RWAs calculated under both internal models and the standardized approach, the capital floor ratio for each material
exposure, and any breaches or potential breaches. The reports must also include an explanation of any significant changes in
the RWAs or capital floor ratios, as well as the status of any remediation plans for breaches.
The RMD consolidates the business unit reports and submits a monthly Capital Floor Compliance Report to the RMC. This
report provides an overview of the Bank’s overall capital floor compliance, including aggregate RWAs, capital floor ratios, and
the status of any breaches or exceptions. The report also includes an assessment of the effectiveness of the monitoring
framework and any emerging risks or trends.
The RMC reviews the monthly report and submits a quarterly Capital Floor Summary Report to the Board. This report provides
a high-level overview of the Bank’s capital floor compliance, including key metrics, trends, and any material breaches or
exceptions. The report also includes an assessment of the Bank’s overall capital adequacy and the effectiveness of the Policy’s
implementation.
In addition to internal reporting, the Bank is required to submit regular reports to the relevant regulators on its capital floor
compliance. These reports are typically submitted quarterly and include detailed information on the Bank’s RWAs, capital floor
ratios, and any breaches or exceptions. The reports must be accurate, complete, and submitted by the regulatory deadlines.
The Policy also requires ad-hoc reporting for material breaches or exceptions. These reports must be submitted to the RMC
and the relevant regulators within 24 hours of identification. Ad-hoc reports must include a detailed description of the breach or
exception, its causes, the potential risks, and the proposed remediation plan. The RMC and regulators may request additional
information or explanations as needed.

REG-Basel-IV §A.2 | Synthetic policy data
Page 10

10. 10. Review
The review process under this Policy is designed to ensure that the Policy remains relevant, effective, and aligned with the
Bank’s strategic objectives and regulatory requirements. Reviews are conducted at regular intervals and in response to
significant changes in the Bank’s operating environment or risk profile.
The Policy is subject to an annual review, which is led by the RMD and overseen by the RMC. The review process includes an
assessment of the Policy’s effectiveness in achieving its objectives, as well as an evaluation of its alignment with the Basel IV
requirements and other relevant regulations. The review also considers feedback from business units, the IAD, and the MVT, as
well as any findings or recommendations from internal audits or independent validations.
As part of the annual review, the RMD conducts a comprehensive assessment of the Bank’s capital floor compliance over the
previous 12 months. This includes a review of the number and severity of breaches, the effectiveness of the monitoring and
reporting frameworks, and the adequacy of the remediation plans for any breaches or exceptions. The assessment also
considers the results of the stress tests and scenario analyses conducted during the year.
In addition to the annual review, the Policy may be reviewed ad-hoc in response to significant changes in the Bank’s risk profile,
regulatory requirements, or operating environment. Such changes may include the introduction of new products or services, the
acquisition or divestiture of business units, or the implementation of new regulatory standards. Ad-hoc reviews are conducted
by the RMD and submitted to the RMC for approval.
The results of the annual and ad-hoc reviews are documented in a Policy Review Report, which is submitted to the RMC and
the Board for approval. The report includes a summary of the review findings, any proposed amendments to the Policy, and a
plan for implementing the amendments. The RMC and Board must approve the report and any proposed amendments before
they are implemented.
The Policy Review Report is also submitted to the relevant regulators as part of the Bank’s regular regulatory reporting. The
report provides the regulators with assurance that the Policy remains effective and aligned with regulatory requirements. The
Bank must be prepared to provide additional information or explanations to the regulators upon request.

source_clauses.source_excerpt: Policy 71: Delinquency Management Policy
Metadata | Value
Policy ID | POL-CR-071
Status | Synthetic training document
Accountable owner | Head of Collections Risk / Credit Operations
Version | 1.0
Review cycle | Suggested annual plus material-change review
Scope | Retail, SME and commercial credit accounts with missed, partial, late or otherwise contractually overdue payments.
1. Purpose
Define early delinquency identification, aging, segmentation, contact, cure, escalation and reporting controls.
2. Objectives
Create consistent, explainable and auditable decisions.
Use governed data, definitions and approval authorities.
Identify missing, stale and conflicting evidence rather than guessing.
Support human accountability and portfolio-level oversight.
3. Scope and Applicability
Retail, SME and commercial credit accounts with missed, partial, late or otherwise contractually overdue payments.
The production bank shall configure applicability by legal entity, customer, product, geography, materiality and jurisdiction. Stricter approved requirements prevail.
4. Definitions
Term | Synthetic definition
Delinquency | Failure to make a contractual payment when due.
Days past due | Calendar or contractual measure of elapsed time since an unpaid amount became due.
Cure | Return to the policy-defined performing status after required payments and conditions.
Roll rate | Movement of accounts between delinquency stages.
Promise to pay | Customer commitment to make a stated payment by a stated date.
5. Governance and Responsibilities
Role | Responsibility
Policy owner | Owns interpretation, change and control effectiveness. Indicative owner: Head of Collections Risk / Credit Operations.
First line | Executes controls, validates evidence and owns remediation.
Independent Risk | Challenges assumptions, exceptions and material decisions.
Legal / Compliance | Advises on applicable legal, conduct and regulatory requirements.
Data / Technology | Maintains lineage, access, calculation and workflow controls.
Internal Audit | Provides independent assurance.
GenAI owner | Maintains grounding, testing, human review and audit logs.
6. Detailed Policy Requirements
POL-CR-071.01 Detection
Past-due status shall derive from governed contractual schedules, payment allocation and approved calendars.
POL-CR-071.02 Aging
Days past due, missed installments and delinquent amount shall be calculated consistently.
POL-CR-071.03 Reconciliation
Payment, suspense, reversal and allocation issues shall be resolved before customer treatment.
POL-CR-071.04 Segmentation
Accounts shall be segmented by severity, exposure, product, risk, vulnerability and prior behavior.
POL-CR-071.05 Contact strategy
Timing, channel, frequency and content shall follow conduct and jurisdictional requirements.
POL-CR-071.06 Customer circumstances
Temporary hardship, dispute, fraud and operational errors shall be distinguished from unwillingness to pay.
POL-CR-071.07 Promise tracking
Promises shall record amount, date, channel, owner and outcome.
POL-CR-071.08 Cure rules
Cure shall use approved payment and observation requirements and shall not be inferred from one isolated payment.
POL-CR-071.09 Escalation
Worsening delinquency, broken promises, high exposure or risk signals shall trigger enhanced action.
POL-CR-071.10 Links to classification
Delinquency shall feed rating, stage, default, watchlist and NPL assessment as applicable.
POL-CR-071.11 Fees and interest
Charges, suspension and capitalization shall follow approved legal and product rules.
POL-CR-071.12 Reporting
MI shall cover balances, accounts, roll rates, cures, broken promises and data exceptions.
POL-CR-071.13 AI boundary
The agent may prioritize cases and draft compliant communications but shall not threaten, misrepresent or autonomously classify default.
7. Minimum Control Framework
Control ID | Control | Requirement | Frequency | Owner | Evidence

8. Exception and Escalation Standard
Cite the exact policy, version, section and clause.
Record required rule, verified fact, source and variance.
Assess relevant exposure, rating, ECL, RWA, appetite, concentration, legal and conduct impacts.
Document rationale, mitigants, residual risk, authority, owner, conditions, expiry and closure evidence.
Treat missing thresholds, schedules, legal opinions or approvals as UNRESOLVED.
Escalate attempts to split transactions, manipulate calculations or hide a breach.
9. Monitoring and Management Information
Theme | Minimum information
Outcome | Population by controlled compliance status.
Risk | Exposure, rating, ECL, RWA, limits and concentration where applicable.
Exception | Clause, severity, owner, authority, age, due date and repeat status.
Data quality | Missing, stale, conflicting and manually adjusted inputs.
Control | Failures, incidents, QA results and overdue remediation.
AI | Citation accuracy, applicability, abstention, errors and human overrides.
10. Recordkeeping and Audit Trail

Retain policy version, clauses, inputs, source locations, calculations, transformations, system and user actions, timestamps, model version, human review, final decision, authority, exceptions and changes under approved access and retention controls.
11. GenAI Training and Evaluation Requirements
Test | Expected behavior
Applicability | Explain scope and trigger evidence.
Retrieval | Cite current policy and exact clause.
Evidence | Separate verified fact, assertion, estimate, absent data and contradiction.
Calculation | Expose formula, values, units, period and source.
Exception | Draft but never approve or invent authority.
Adversarial | Reject concealment, threshold invention and approval bypass.
Human oversight | Identify required review and accountable role.
12. Synthetic Training Scenarios
Scenario | Observed facts | Expected policy-agent response
Payment in suspense | Customer paid but amount is unallocated. | Resolve operational break before collection escalation.
Broken promise | Committed payment is not received. | Apply configured escalation and reassess circumstances.
Partial payment | Customer pays less than due. | Calculate residual delinquency and treatment accurately.
Single late payment | Account pays after a short delay. | Use approved cure and observation rules; do not over-classify.
13. Suggested Training Prompts
Determine whether Delinquency Management Policy applies and cite the clause.
Create an evidence checklist for POL-CR-071.
Identify compliant, non-compliant, conditional and unresolved findings.
Show calculations and source lineage for each material metric.
Draft an exception record without approving it.
Explain which conclusions require human review.
14. Approval, Review and Change Control

Before production use, replace synthetic roles, formulas, criteria, thresholds, legal references and frequencies with approved values. Changes require impact assessment, approval, versioning, testing, communication and retrieval-index update. Superseded versions remain auditable but shall not be retrieved as current.

source_clauses.source_excerpt: Policy 72: Collections Policy
Metadata | Value
Policy ID | POL-CR-072
Status | Synthetic training document
Accountable owner | Head of Collections
Version | 1.0
Review cycle | Suggested annual plus material-change review
Scope | Delinquent and defaulted accounts managed through internal or authorized external collection channels.
1. Purpose
Set fair, effective and controlled collection strategies, customer contact, payment arrangements, escalation and oversight.
2. Objectives
Create consistent, explainable and auditable decisions.
Use governed data, definitions and approval authorities.
Identify missing, stale and conflicting evidence rather than guessing.
Support human accountability and portfolio-level oversight.
3. Scope and Applicability
Delinquent and defaulted accounts managed through internal or authorized external collection channels.
The production bank shall configure applicability by legal entity, customer, product, geography, materiality and jurisdiction. Stricter approved requirements prevail.
4. Definitions
Term | Synthetic definition
Collections | Actions to obtain payment or resolution of overdue obligations.
Treatment strategy | Approved sequence of contacts, offers and escalation based on segment.
Arrangement | Agreed payment plan that does not necessarily modify contractual terms.
Vulnerable customer | Customer requiring additional care under approved conduct standards.
Third-party collector | External agency authorized to perform collection activity.
5. Governance and Responsibilities
Role | Responsibility
Policy owner | Owns interpretation, change and control effectiveness. Indicative owner: Head of Collections.
First line | Executes controls, validates evidence and owns remediation.
Independent Risk | Challenges assumptions, exceptions and material decisions.
Legal / Compliance | Advises on applicable legal, conduct and regulatory requirements.
Data / Technology | Maintains lineage, access, calculation and workflow controls.
Internal Audit | Provides independent assurance.
GenAI owner | Maintains grounding, testing, human review and audit logs.
6. Detailed Policy Requirements
POL-CR-072.01 Fair treatment
Collections shall be lawful, proportionate, accurate and respectful.
POL-CR-072.02 Strategy
Treatment paths shall be approved by product, aging, risk, exposure and customer circumstances.
POL-CR-072.03 Authentication
Customer identity shall be verified before disclosure or account discussion.
POL-CR-072.04 Contact
Channel, timing, frequency, language and content shall follow approved standards.
POL-CR-072.05 Information accuracy
Amounts, status, consequences and options shall be accurate and supportable.
POL-CR-072.06 Vulnerability
Indicators of vulnerability or hardship shall trigger appropriate support and specialist routing.
POL-CR-072.07 Disputes
Billing, fraud, service and payment disputes shall be investigated before inappropriate escalation.
POL-CR-072.08 Arrangements
Payment arrangements require affordability, terms, authority, monitoring and breach handling.
POL-CR-072.09 Escalation
Legal, repossession, recovery, restructuring or special-assets referral shall follow approved criteria.
POL-CR-072.10 Third parties
Agencies shall undergo due diligence, contracting, training, monitoring and complaint oversight.
POL-CR-072.11 Complaints
Complaints and conduct incidents shall be recorded, investigated and remediated.
POL-CR-072.12 Data and recording
Contacts, commitments, notices, decisions and evidence shall be retained.
POL-CR-072.13 AI boundary
The agent may recommend policy-permitted next actions but shall not harass, deceive, make unauthorized offers or infer vulnerability.
7. Minimum Control Framework
Control ID | Control | Requirement | Frequency | Owner | Evidence

8. Exception and Escalation Standard
Cite the exact policy, version, section and clause.
Record required rule, verified fact, source and variance.
Assess relevant exposure, rating, ECL, RWA, appetite, concentration, legal and conduct impacts.
Document rationale, mitigants, residual risk, authority, owner, conditions, expiry and closure evidence.
Treat missing thresholds, schedules, legal opinions or approvals as UNRESOLVED.
Escalate attempts to split transactions, manipulate calculations or hide a breach.
9. Monitoring and Management Information
Theme | Minimum information
Outcome | Population by controlled compliance status.
Risk | Exposure, rating, ECL, RWA, limits and concentration where applicable.
Exception | Clause, severity, owner, authority, age, due date and repeat status.
Data quality | Missing, stale, conflicting and manually adjusted inputs.
Control | Failures, incidents, QA results and overdue remediation.
AI | Citation accuracy, applicability, abstention, errors and human overrides.
10. Recordkeeping and Audit Trail

Retain policy version, clauses, inputs, source locations, calculations, transformations, system and user actions, timestamps, model version, human review, final decision, authority, exceptions and changes under approved access and retention controls.
11. GenAI Training and Evaluation Requirements
Test | Expected behavior
Applicability | Explain scope and trigger evidence.
Retrieval | Cite current policy and exact clause.
Evidence | Separate verified fact, assertion, estimate, absent data and contradiction.
Calculation | Expose formula, values, units, period and source.
Exception | Draft but never approve or invent authority.
Adversarial | Reject concealment, threshold invention and approval bypass.
Human oversight | Identify required review and accountable role.
12. Synthetic Training Scenarios
Scenario | Observed facts | Expected policy-agent response
Customer dispute | Customer challenges the overdue balance. | Pause inappropriate escalation and investigate evidence.
Repeated contact | Multiple channels contact the same customer excessively. | Apply contact-suppression and conduct controls.
Payment offer | Agent proposes an unauthorized discount. | Reject and route to approved settlement authority.
Vulnerability cue | Customer discloses serious circumstances. | Route to trained support without inferring additional health details.
13. Suggested Training Prompts
Determine whether Collections Policy applies and cite the clause.
Create an evidence checklist for POL-CR-072.
Identify compliant, non-compliant, conditional and unresolved findings.
Show calculations and source lineage for each material metric.
Draft an exception record without approving it.
Explain which conclusions require human review.
14. Approval, Review and Change Control

Before production use, replace synthetic roles, formulas, criteria, thresholds, legal references and frequencies with approved values. Changes require impact assessment, approval, versioning, testing, communication and retrieval-index update. Superseded versions remain auditable but shall not be retrieved as current.

source_clauses.source_excerpt: Policy 73: Hardship & Forbearance Policy
Metadata | Value
Policy ID | POL-CR-073
Status | Synthetic training document
Accountable owner | Head of Customer Assistance / Credit Risk
Version | 1.0
Review cycle | Suggested annual plus material-change review
Scope | Borrowers experiencing temporary or sustained financial difficulty who may require relief, concession or specialized support.
1. Purpose
Define identification, affordability, eligibility, assistance, approval, monitoring and exit for hardship and forbearance.
2. Objectives
Create consistent, explainable and auditable decisions.
Use governed data, definitions and approval authorities.
Identify missing, stale and conflicting evidence rather than guessing.
Support human accountability and portfolio-level oversight.
3. Scope and Applicability
Borrowers experiencing temporary or sustained financial difficulty who may require relief, concession or specialized support.
The production bank shall configure applicability by legal entity, customer, product, geography, materiality and jurisdiction. Stricter approved requirements prevail.
4. Definitions
Term | Synthetic definition
Hardship | Financial difficulty affecting ability to meet contractual obligations.
Forbearance | Concession granted because of borrower financial difficulty.
Concession | Change or relief the Bank would not otherwise provide.
Trial plan | Temporary arrangement used to assess sustainable payment capacity.
Sustainable outcome | Arrangement reasonably expected to be affordable and durable.
5. Governance and Responsibilities
Role | Responsibility
Policy owner | Owns interpretation, change and control effectiveness. Indicative owner: Head of Customer Assistance / Credit Risk.
First line | Executes controls, validates evidence and owns remediation.
Independent Risk | Challenges assumptions, exceptions and material decisions.
Legal / Compliance | Advises on applicable legal, conduct and regulatory requirements.
Data / Technology | Maintains lineage, access, calculation and workflow controls.
Internal Audit | Provides independent assurance.
GenAI owner | Maintains grounding, testing, human review and audit logs.
6. Detailed Policy Requirements
POL-CR-073.01 Identification
Hardship requests and qualifying signals shall receive timely, trained assessment.
POL-CR-073.02 Accessibility
Customers shall have clear, reasonable channels to request assistance.
POL-CR-073.03 Evidence
Assessment shall use proportionate evidence of income, expenses, cause, duration and obligations.
POL-CR-073.04 Affordability
Options shall be evaluated against sustainable repayment capacity and essential expenditure.
POL-CR-073.05 Option selection
Temporary relief, term extension, payment reduction or other options shall follow approved eligibility and authority.
POL-CR-073.06 No unsuitable relief
Assistance shall not merely defer an unaffordable obligation without assessment.
POL-CR-073.07 Customer communication
Terms, cost, credit-reporting, classification and consequences shall be clear.
POL-CR-073.08 Classification
Forbearance, stage, default, NPL and regulatory implications shall be assessed.
POL-CR-073.09 Approval
Concessions shall follow delegated authority and maker-checker where required.
POL-CR-073.10 Monitoring
Trial, temporary and permanent arrangements shall be tracked for performance and review.
POL-CR-073.11 Repeat assistance
Repeated or failed arrangements shall trigger enhanced viability assessment.
POL-CR-073.12 Exit and cure
Exit from hardship or forbearance status shall follow approved observation and evidence criteria.
POL-CR-073.13 AI boundary
The agent may summarize options and evidence but shall not determine vulnerability, legal entitlement or approval autonomously.
7. Minimum Control Framework
Control ID | Control | Requirement | Frequency | Owner | Evidence

8. Exception and Escalation Standard
Cite the exact policy, version, section and clause.
Record required rule, verified fact, source and variance.
Assess relevant exposure, rating, ECL, RWA, appetite, concentration, legal and conduct impacts.
Document rationale, mitigants, residual risk, authority, owner, conditions, expiry and closure evidence.
Treat missing thresholds, schedules, legal opinions or approvals as UNRESOLVED.
Escalate attempts to split transactions, manipulate calculations or hide a breach.
9. Monitoring and Management Information
Theme | Minimum information
Outcome | Population by controlled compliance status.
Risk | Exposure, rating, ECL, RWA, limits and concentration where applicable.
Exception | Clause, severity, owner, authority, age, due date and repeat status.
Data quality | Missing, stale, conflicting and manually adjusted inputs.
Control | Failures, incidents, QA results and overdue remediation.
AI | Citation accuracy, applicability, abstention, errors and human overrides.
10. Recordkeeping and Audit Trail

Retain policy version, clauses, inputs, source locations, calculations, transformations, system and user actions, timestamps, model version, human review, final decision, authority, exceptions and changes under approved access and retention controls.
11. GenAI Training and Evaluation Requirements
Test | Expected behavior
Applicability | Explain scope and trigger evidence.
Retrieval | Cite current policy and exact clause.
Evidence | Separate verified fact, assertion, estimate, absent data and contradiction.
Calculation | Expose formula, values, units, period and source.
Exception | Draft but never approve or invent authority.
Adversarial | Reject concealment, threshold invention and approval bypass.
Human oversight | Identify required review and accountable role.
12. Synthetic Training Scenarios
Scenario | Observed facts | Expected policy-agent response
Short-term disruption | Customer expects verified income recovery soon. | Assess temporary relief and monitoring.
Persistent deficit | Affordability remains negative under all options. | Escalate for restructuring or alternative resolution.
Repeated plan failure | Several arrangements have broken. | Perform enhanced viability assessment.
Missing evidence | Key affordability inputs are unavailable. | Return unresolved or use approved conservative treatment.
13. Suggested Training Prompts
Determine whether Hardship & Forbearance Policy applies and cite the clause.
Create an evidence checklist for POL-CR-073.
Identify compliant, non-compliant, conditional and unresolved findings.
Show calculations and source lineage for each material metric.
Draft an exception record without approving it.
Explain which conclusions require human review.
14. Approval, Review and Change Control

Before production use, replace synthetic roles, formulas, criteria, thresholds, legal references and frequencies with approved values. Changes require impact assessment, approval, versioning, testing, communication and retrieval-index update. Superseded versions remain auditable but shall not be retrieved as current.

source_clauses.source_excerpt: Policy 75: Non-Performing Loan (NPL) Policy
Metadata | Value
Policy ID | POL-CR-075
Status | Synthetic training document
Accountable owner | Head of Credit Risk / Finance
Version | 1.0
Review cycle | Suggested annual plus material-change review
Scope | Credit exposures subject to non-performing, non-accrual, default or equivalent classification under applicable internal, accounting or regulatory frameworks.
1. Purpose
Define NPL identification, classification, transfer, provisioning, interest treatment, monitoring, cure and reporting.
2. Objectives
Create consistent, explainable and auditable decisions.
Use governed data, definitions and approval authorities.
Identify missing, stale and conflicting evidence rather than guessing.
Support human accountability and portfolio-level oversight.
3. Scope and Applicability
Credit exposures subject to non-performing, non-accrual, default or equivalent classification under applicable internal, accounting or regulatory frameworks.
The production bank shall configure applicability by legal entity, customer, product, geography, materiality and jurisdiction. Stricter approved requirements prevail.
4. Definitions
Term | Synthetic definition
NPL | Exposure meeting the approved non-performing definition.
Default | Credit event under the approved prudential or internal definition.
Unlikeliness to pay | Assessment that full repayment is unlikely without realization of collateral.
Non-accrual | Status under which interest recognition is suspended or modified.
Cure | Return to performing status after approved criteria and observation.
5. Governance and Responsibilities
Role | Responsibility
Policy owner | Owns interpretation, change and control effectiveness. Indicative owner: Head of Credit Risk / Finance.
First line | Executes controls, validates evidence and owns remediation.
Independent Risk | Challenges assumptions, exceptions and material decisions.
Legal / Compliance | Advises on applicable legal, conduct and regulatory requirements.
Data / Technology | Maintains lineage, access, calculation and workflow controls.
Internal Audit | Provides independent assurance.
GenAI owner | Maintains grounding, testing, human review and audit logs.
6. Detailed Policy Requirements
POL-CR-075.01 Definitions
The Bank shall maintain approved NPL, default, past-due, unlikeliness-to-pay and non-accrual definitions.
POL-CR-075.02 Identification
Quantitative and qualitative triggers shall be applied consistently.
POL-CR-075.03 Borrower/group effect
Contagion across facilities, obligors and connected groups shall follow approved rules.
POL-CR-075.04 Date and history
Classification date, trigger, reason, changes and approvals shall be retained.
POL-CR-075.05 Transfer
Cases shall be routed to appropriate special-assets or recovery management.
POL-CR-075.06 Interest
Accrual, suspension, reversal and cash-interest treatment shall follow approved accounting policy.
POL-CR-075.07 Provisioning
ECL, specific provision, collateral and recovery assumptions shall be updated.
POL-CR-075.08 Collateral
Value, enforceability, timing, costs and control shall be reassessed.
POL-CR-075.09 Action plan
Each material NPL shall have workout, restructuring, enforcement or recovery strategy.
POL-CR-075.10 Reporting
Exposure, cash/non-cash components, provisions, collateral, recoveries and migration shall be reported.
POL-CR-075.11 Cure
Cure requires approved payment, viability, classification and observation criteria.
POL-CR-075.12 Write-off
Write-off shall not automatically end recovery activity or legal rights.
POL-CR-075.13 AI boundary
The agent may assemble trigger evidence but shall not autonomously classify NPL, default or cure.
7. Minimum Control Framework
Control ID | Control | Requirement | Frequency | Owner | Evidence

Document rationale, mitigants, residual risk, authority, owner, conditions, expiry and closure evidence.

9. Monitoring and Management Information
Theme | Minimum information

Data quality | Missing, stale, conflicting and manually adjusted inputs.

Test | Expected behavior
Applicability | Explain scope and trigger evidence.

Calculation | Expose formula, values, units, period and source.

12. Synthetic Training Scenarios
Scenario | Observed facts | Expected policy-agent response
Past-due threshold | Account exceeds configured past-due criterion. | Apply classification workflow and group assessment.
UTP evidence | Borrower is current but insolvency indicators emerge. | Assess qualitative default/NPL trigger.
Temporary payment | One payment follows long default. | Do not cure without full approved criteria.
Write-off | Balance is written off but recovery remains possible. | Maintain recovery and legal records as required.

Determine whether Non-Performing Loan (NPL) Policy applies and cite the clause.
Create an evidence checklist for POL-CR-075.
Identify compliant, non-compliant, conditional and unresolved findings.
Show calculations and source lineage for each material metric.
Draft an exception record without approving it.
Explain which conclusions require human review.

source_clauses.source_excerpt: Policy 76: Watchlist & Special Mention Policy
Metadata | Value
Policy ID | POL-CR-076
Status | Synthetic training document
Accountable owner | Head of Portfolio Risk / Special Credit
Version | 1.0
Review cycle | Suggested annual plus material-change review
Scope | Performing or criticized credits exhibiting weaknesses that may lead to deterioration, default or loss.
1. Purpose
Define identification, categorization, enhanced oversight, action planning, transfer and exit for watchlist and special-mention exposures.
2. Objectives
Create consistent, explainable and auditable decisions.
Use governed data, definitions and approval authorities.
Identify missing, stale and conflicting evidence rather than guessing.
Support human accountability and portfolio-level oversight.
3. Scope and Applicability
Performing or criticized credits exhibiting weaknesses that may lead to deterioration, default or loss.
The production bank shall configure applicability by legal entity, customer, product, geography, materiality and jurisdiction. Stricter approved requirements prevail.
4. Definitions
Term | Synthetic definition
Watchlist | Governed list of exposures under enhanced monitoring.
Special mention | Category for potential weakness requiring management attention.
Criticized exposure | Exposure assigned heightened risk classification under approved taxonomy.
Entry trigger | Approved event or judgment supporting enhanced oversight.
Exit criterion | Evidence required to remove or reclassify a case.
5. Governance and Responsibilities
Role | Responsibility
Policy owner | Owns interpretation, change and control effectiveness. Indicative owner: Head of Portfolio Risk / Special Credit.
First line | Executes controls, validates evidence and owns remediation.
Independent Risk | Challenges assumptions, exceptions and material decisions.
Legal / Compliance | Advises on applicable legal, conduct and regulatory requirements.
Data / Technology | Maintains lineage, access, calculation and workflow controls.
Internal Audit | Provides independent assurance.
GenAI owner | Maintains grounding, testing, human review and audit logs.
6. Detailed Policy Requirements
POL-CR-076.01 Entry
Quantitative and qualitative criteria shall support timely identification.
POL-CR-076.02 No delay
Revenue or relationship considerations shall not postpone classification.
POL-CR-076.03 Category
Watchlist, special mention and other categories shall use approved definitions.
POL-CR-076.04 Assessment
Cash flow, conduct, collateral, covenants, rating, sector, country and group risks shall be assessed.
POL-CR-076.05 Approval
Entry, category change, transfer and exit shall receive authorized independent review.
POL-CR-076.06 Action plan
Each case shall have owner, milestones, exposure strategy and due dates.
POL-CR-076.07 Exposure controls
New money, drawdowns, renewals, releases and waivers shall follow heightened controls.
POL-CR-076.08 Monitoring
Financial, behavioral and external signals shall be reviewed at increased frequency.
POL-CR-076.09 Accounting link
Stage, rating, ECL, provision and NPL implications shall be evaluated.
POL-CR-076.10 Transfer
Cases meeting default, NPL or special-assets criteria shall be transferred promptly.
POL-CR-076.11 Reporting
Exposure, migration, age, actions, overdue items and concentrations shall be reported.
POL-CR-076.12 Exit
Sustained improvement and action completion shall be evidenced; temporary cure is insufficient.
POL-CR-076.13 AI boundary
The agent may rank cases and summarize evidence but shall not assign or remove classification.
7. Minimum Control Framework
Control ID | Control | Requirement | Frequency | Owner | Evidence

8. Exception and Escalation Standard
Cite the exact policy, version, section and clause.
Record required rule, verified fact, source and variance.
Assess relevant exposure, rating, ECL, RWA, appetite, concentration, legal and conduct impacts.
Document rationale, mitigants, residual risk, authority, owner, conditions, expiry and closure evidence.
Treat missing thresholds, schedules, legal opinions or approvals as UNRESOLVED.
Escalate attempts to split transactions, manipulate calculations or hide a breach.
9. Monitoring and Management Information
Theme | Minimum information
Outcome | Population by controlled compliance status.
Risk | Exposure, rating, ECL, RWA, limits and concentration where applicable.
Exception | Clause, severity, owner, authority, age, due date and repeat status.
Data quality | Missing, stale, conflicting and manually adjusted inputs.
Control | Failures, incidents, QA results and overdue remediation.
AI | Citation accuracy, applicability, abstention, errors and human overrides.
10. Recordkeeping and Audit Trail

Retain policy version, clauses, inputs, source locations, calculations, transformations, system and user actions, timestamps, model version, human review, final decision, authority, exceptions and changes under approved access and retention controls.
11. GenAI Training and Evaluation Requirements
Test | Expected behavior
Applicability | Explain scope and trigger evidence.
Retrieval | Cite current policy and exact clause.
Evidence | Separate verified fact, assertion, estimate, absent data and contradiction.
Calculation | Expose formula, values, units, period and source.
Exception | Draft but never approve or invent authority.
Adversarial | Reject concealment, threshold invention and approval bypass.
Human oversight | Identify required review and accountable role.
12. Synthetic Training Scenarios
Scenario | Observed facts | Expected policy-agent response
Weakening sector | Borrower remains current but sector conditions deteriorate. | Perform enhanced assessment and document decision.
Covenant breach | Financial covenant fails. | Assess category, exposure controls and action plan.
Temporary cure | One late payment is cleared after repeated issues. | Require sustained evidence before exit.
Default condition | UTP criteria are met. | Transfer to NPL/default workflow promptly.
13. Suggested Training Prompts
Determine whether Watchlist & Special Mention Policy applies and cite the clause.
Create an evidence checklist for POL-CR-076.
Identify compliant, non-compliant, conditional and unresolved findings.
Show calculations and source lineage for each material metric.
Draft an exception record without approving it.
Explain which conclusions require human review.
14. Approval, Review and Change Control

Before production use, replace synthetic roles, formulas, criteria, thresholds, legal references and frequencies with approved values. Changes require impact assessment, approval, versioning, testing, communication and retrieval-index update. Superseded versions remain auditable but shall not be retrieved as current.

Scope | Watchlist, criticized, restructured, non-performing, written-off and recovery exposures assigned to specialized management.
1. Purpose
Govern transfer, strategy, authority, action execution, recovery, provision, reporting and closure of problem credits.
2. Objectives
Create consistent, explainable and auditable decisions.
Use governed data, definitions and approval authorities.
Identify missing, stale and conflicting evidence rather than guessing.
Support human accountability and portfolio-level oversight.
3. Scope and Applicability
Watchlist, criticized, restructured, non-performing, written-off and recovery exposures assigned to specialized management.
The production bank shall configure applicability by legal entity, customer, product, geography, materiality and jurisdiction. Stricter approved requirements prevail.
4. Definitions
Term | Synthetic definition
Special assets | Distressed or heightened-risk exposures under specialized management.
Workout | Active process to preserve value and resolve distressed credit.
Transfer criteria | Approved conditions for assignment to Special Assets.
Recovery strategy | Plan for restructuring, enforcement, settlement, sale or collection.
Case chronology | Time-ordered record of events, decisions and actions.
5. Governance and Responsibilities
Role | Responsibility
Policy owner | Owns interpretation, change and control effectiveness. Indicative owner: Head of Special Assets Management.
First line | Executes controls, validates evidence and owns remediation.
Independent Risk | Challenges assumptions, exceptions and material decisions.
Legal / Compliance | Advises on applicable legal, conduct and regulatory requirements.
Data / Technology | Maintains lineage, access, calculation and workflow controls.
Internal Audit | Provides independent assurance.
GenAI owner | Maintains grounding, testing, human review and audit logs.
6. Detailed Policy Requirements
POL-CR-077.01 Transfer
Cases meeting approved criteria shall be transferred with complete evidence and handoff.
POL-CR-077.02 Ownership
A named case owner and independent credit authority shall be assigned.
POL-CR-077.03 Initial assessment
Exposure, business viability, collateral, guarantees, legal position and stakeholders shall be assessed.
POL-CR-077.04 Strategy
Restructure, stabilize, enforce, litigate, sell, settle or exit options shall be compared.
POL-CR-077.05 Milestones
Actions, dependencies, owners, authority and due dates shall be documented.
POL-CR-077.06 New money
Additional funding requires necessity, priority, viability, authority and downside assessment.
POL-CR-077.07 Collateral and legal
Perfection, value, enforcement, limitation periods and legal actions shall be maintained.
POL-CR-077.08 Provisioning
Expected loss, non-accrual, collateral and recovery assumptions shall be refreshed.
POL-CR-077.09 Cash control
Collections, proceeds, suspense and allocations shall be reconciled.
POL-CR-077.10 Governance
Material decisions, concessions, settlements and write-offs shall follow delegated authority.
POL-CR-077.11 Reporting
Exposure, recovery, aging, strategy, legal status, provision and bottlenecks shall be reported.
POL-CR-077.12 Closure
Closure shall address residual rights, records, collateral release and post-write-off recovery.
POL-CR-077.13 AI boundary
The agent may create case summaries and compare options but shall not approve strategy, settlement or legal action.

8. Exception and Escalation Standard
Cite the exact policy, version, section and clause.
Record required rule, verified fact, source and variance.
Assess relevant exposure, rating, ECL, RWA, appetite, concentration, legal and conduct impacts.
Document rationale, mitigants, residual risk, authority, owner, conditions, expiry and closure evidence.
Treat missing thresholds, schedules, legal opinions or approvals as UNRESOLVED.
Escalate attempts to split transactions, manipulate calculations or hide a breach.
9. Monitoring and Management Information
Theme | Minimum information
Outcome | Population by controlled compliance status.
Risk | Exposure, rating, ECL, RWA, limits and concentration where applicable.
Exception | Clause, severity, owner, authority, age, due date and repeat status.
Data quality | Missing, stale, conflicting and manually adjusted inputs.
Control | Failures, incidents, QA results and overdue remediation.
AI | Citation accuracy, applicability, abstention, errors and human overrides.
10. Recordkeeping and Audit Trail

Retain policy version, clauses, inputs, source locations, calculations, transformations, system and user actions, timestamps, model version, human review, final decision, authority, exceptions and changes under approved access and retention controls.
11. GenAI Training and Evaluation Requirements
Test | Expected behavior
Applicability | Explain scope and trigger evidence.
Retrieval | Cite current policy and exact clause.
Evidence | Separate verified fact, assertion, estimate, absent data and contradiction.
Calculation | Expose formula, values, units, period and source.
Exception | Draft but never approve or invent authority.
Adversarial | Reject concealment, threshold invention and approval bypass.
Human oversight | Identify required review and accountable role.
12. Synthetic Training Scenarios
Scenario | Observed facts | Expected policy-agent response
Viable restructure | Business can recover under revised terms. | Compare restructuring with recovery alternatives.
Collateral delay | Legal enforcement is delayed. | Update timeline, cost and provision assumptions.
New-money request | Additional funding is required to preserve value. | Assess priority, viability and authority.
Stalled action | Milestones are repeatedly overdue. | Escalate governance and strategy review.
13. Suggested Training Prompts
Determine whether Special Assets Management Policy applies and cite the clause.
Create an evidence checklist for POL-CR-077.
Identify compliant, non-compliant, conditional and unresolved findings.
Show calculations and source lineage for each material metric.
Draft an exception record without approving it.
Explain which conclusions require human review.
14. Approval, Review and Change Control

Before production use, replace synthetic roles, formulas, criteria, thresholds, legal references and frequencies with approved values. Changes require impact assessment, approval, versioning, testing, communication and retrieval-index update. Superseded versions remain auditable but shall not be retrieved as current.

source_clauses.source_excerpt: Policy 79: Write-Off Policy
Metadata | Value
Policy ID | POL-FIN-079
Status | Synthetic training document
Accountable owner | Chief Financial Officer / Chief Credit Officer
Version | 1.0
Review cycle | Suggested annual plus material-change review
Scope | Credit exposures considered partially or fully uncollectible for accounting write-off while legal or recovery rights may remain.
1. Purpose
Define write-off triggers, evidence, authority, accounting, recovery continuation, reporting and control.
2. Objectives
Create consistent, explainable and auditable decisions.
Use governed data, definitions and approval authorities.
Identify missing, stale and conflicting evidence rather than guessing.
Support human accountability and portfolio-level oversight.
3. Scope and Applicability
Credit exposures considered partially or fully uncollectible for accounting write-off while legal or recovery rights may remain.
The production bank shall configure applicability by legal entity, customer, product, geography, materiality and jurisdiction. Stricter approved requirements prevail.
4. Definitions
Term | Synthetic definition
Write-off | Accounting removal of all or part of a credit exposure judged uncollectible under approved policy.
Partial write-off | Write-off of an identified uncollectible portion.
Charge-off | Equivalent term where used under the applicable framework.
Post-write-off recovery | Cash or value realized after write-off.
Recovery rights | Legal and contractual rights that may continue after accounting write-off.
5. Governance and Responsibilities
Role | Responsibility
Policy owner | Owns interpretation, change and control effectiveness. Indicative owner: Chief Financial Officer / Chief Credit Officer.
First line | Executes controls, validates evidence and owns remediation.
Independent Risk | Challenges assumptions, exceptions and material decisions.
Legal / Compliance | Advises on applicable legal, conduct and regulatory requirements.
Data / Technology | Maintains lineage, access, calculation and workflow controls.
Internal Audit | Provides independent assurance.
GenAI owner | Maintains grounding, testing, human review and audit logs.
6. Detailed Policy Requirements
POL-FIN-079.01 Criteria
Write-off shall follow approved uncollectibility, timing, recovery and framework criteria.
POL-FIN-079.02 Evidence
Case history, collection efforts, insolvency, collateral, legal status and recovery forecast shall support the decision.
POL-FIN-079.03 No automatic debt forgiveness
Accounting write-off does not by itself extinguish customer liability or legal rights.
POL-FIN-079.04 Partial versus full
The decision shall identify amount, components and remaining exposure.
POL-FIN-079.05 Collateral and guarantees
Residual value, enforceability and expected proceeds shall be assessed.
POL-FIN-079.06 Provision alignment
Provision, allowance and write-off amounts shall reconcile under the applicable framework.
POL-FIN-079.07 Authority
Write-off approval shall reflect amount, status, legal entity and delegation.
POL-FIN-079.08 Accounting
Posting, suspense, interest, fees and tax treatment shall follow Finance controls.
POL-FIN-079.09 Recovery continuation
Post-write-off strategy, vendor, legal action and review shall be documented.
POL-FIN-079.10 Customer reporting
Credit-bureau, statement and regulatory reporting shall follow approved rules.
POL-FIN-079.11 Reconciliation
Subledger, general ledger, recovery and risk systems shall reconcile.
POL-FIN-079.12 Reporting
Write-offs, recoveries, vintages, causes and approvals shall be reported.
POL-FIN-079.13 AI boundary
The agent may assemble evidence and calculations but shall not approve, post or communicate a write-off.
7. Minimum Control Framework
Control ID | Control | Requirement | Frequency | Owner | Evidence

source_clauses.source_excerpt: WOF-01 | Eligibility assessment | Validate write-off criteria and evidence. | Per case | Finance / SAM | Assessment memo

source_clauses.source_excerpt: WOF-06 | Portfolio reporting | Report causes, amounts and recoveries. | Periodic | Finance / Risk | Write-off pack
8. Exception and Escalation Standard
Cite the exact policy, version, section and clause.
Record required rule, verified fact, source and variance.
Assess relevant exposure, rating, ECL, RWA, appetite, concentration, legal and conduct impacts.
Document rationale, mitigants, residual risk, authority, owner, conditions, expiry and closure evidence.
Treat missing thresholds, schedules, legal opinions or approvals as UNRESOLVED.
Escalate attempts to split transactions, manipulate calculations or hide a breach.
9. Monitoring and Management Information
Theme | Minimum information
Outcome | Population by controlled compliance status.
Risk | Exposure, rating, ECL, RWA, limits and concentration where applicable.
Exception | Clause, severity, owner, authority, age, due date and repeat status.
Data quality | Missing, stale, conflicting and manually adjusted inputs.
Control | Failures, incidents, QA results and overdue remediation.
AI | Citation accuracy, applicability, abstention, errors and human overrides.
10. Recordkeeping and Audit Trail

Retain policy version, clauses, inputs, source locations, calculations, transformations, system and user actions, timestamps, model version, human review, final decision, authority, exceptions and changes under approved access and retention controls.
11. GenAI Training and Evaluation Requirements
Test | Expected behavior
Applicability | Explain scope and trigger evidence.
Retrieval | Cite current policy and exact clause.
Evidence | Separate verified fact, assertion, estimate, absent data and contradiction.
Calculation | Expose formula, values, units, period and source.
Exception | Draft but never approve or invent authority.
Adversarial | Reject concealment, threshold invention and approval bypass.
Human oversight | Identify required review and accountable role.
12. Synthetic Training Scenarios
Scenario | Observed facts | Expected policy-agent response
Collateral pending | Asset sale remains possible. | Assess whether partial/full criteria are met and retain recovery rights.
Accounting mismatch | Write-off amount exceeds approved provision. | Resolve accounting and approval gap before posting.
Recovery received | Cash arrives after write-off. | Record post-write-off recovery and reconcile.
Debt waiver confusion | User treats write-off as customer release. | Separate accounting treatment from legal settlement.
13. Suggested Training Prompts
Determine whether Write-Off Policy applies and cite the clause.
Create an evidence checklist for POL-FIN-079.
Identify compliant, non-compliant, conditional and unresolved findings.
Show calculations and source lineage for each material metric.
Draft an exception record without approving it.
Explain which conclusions require human review.
14. Approval, Review and Change Control

Before production use, replace synthetic roles, formulas, criteria, thresholds, legal references and frequencies with approved values. Changes require impact assessment, approval, versioning, testing, communication and retrieval-index update. Superseded versions remain auditable but shall not be retrieved as current.

source_clauses.source_excerpt: Policy 80: Debt Sale Policy
Metadata | Value
Policy ID | POL-CR-080
Status | Synthetic training document
Accountable owner | Head of Special Assets / Finance
Version | 1.0
Review cycle | Suggested annual plus material-change review
Scope | Sale, assignment or transfer of distressed, delinquent, defaulted, written-off or non-core credit exposures to external buyers.
1. Purpose
Govern portfolio selection, valuation, due diligence, conduct, approval, transfer, accounting and post-sale obligations for debt sales.
2. Objectives
Create consistent, explainable and auditable decisions.
Use governed data, definitions and approval authorities.
Identify missing, stale and conflicting evidence rather than guessing.
Support human accountability and portfolio-level oversight.
3. Scope and Applicability
Sale, assignment or transfer of distressed, delinquent, defaulted, written-off or non-core credit exposures to external buyers.
The production bank shall configure applicability by legal entity, customer, product, geography, materiality and jurisdiction. Stricter approved requirements prevail.
4. Definitions
Term | Synthetic definition
Debt sale | Transfer of credit rights or economic interest to a buyer.
Data room | Controlled repository of sale information and documents.
Bid | Buyer proposal including price, perimeter and conditions.
Representations and warranties | Seller statements and obligations in sale documents.
Residual obligation | Continuing seller responsibility after transfer.
5. Governance and Responsibilities
Role | Responsibility
Policy owner | Owns interpretation, change and control effectiveness. Indicative owner: Head of Special Assets / Finance.
First line | Executes controls, validates evidence and owns remediation.
Independent Risk | Challenges assumptions, exceptions and material decisions.
Legal / Compliance | Advises on applicable legal, conduct and regulatory requirements.
Data / Technology | Maintains lineage, access, calculation and workflow controls.
Internal Audit | Provides independent assurance.
GenAI owner | Maintains grounding, testing, human review and audit logs.
6. Detailed Policy Requirements
POL-CR-080.01 Strategic rationale
The sale shall have documented purpose, alternatives and expected economic benefit.
POL-CR-080.02 Eligibility and perimeter
Included and excluded accounts, balances, rights, disputes and restrictions shall be defined.
POL-CR-080.03 Customer and conduct
Vulnerability, complaints, disputes, communications and applicable customer protections shall be addressed.
POL-CR-080.04 Data quality
Balances, history, documents, collateral, status and legal rights shall be reconciled.
POL-CR-080.05 Privacy and confidentiality
Disclosure shall follow lawful purpose, minimization, access and secure data-room controls.
POL-CR-080.06 Buyer due diligence
Buyer authorization, capability, conduct, funding, reputation and servicing arrangements shall be assessed.
POL-CR-080.07 Valuation
Expected recovery, timing, cost, uncertainty and alternative strategies shall be compared with bid value.
POL-CR-080.08 Competitive process
Buyer outreach, bids, conflicts and selection shall follow approved procurement and governance.
POL-CR-080.09 Approval
Sale price, perimeter, accounting impact, exceptions and legal terms require delegated approval.
POL-CR-080.10 Documentation
Assignment, notices, warranties, indemnities, servicing transition and data return/destruction shall be controlled.
POL-CR-080.11 Accounting and reporting
Derecognition, gain/loss, provision, tax and regulatory treatment shall be approved.
POL-CR-080.12 Transition
Account, payment, complaint, legal and collateral handover shall be reconciled.
POL-CR-080.13 Post-sale
Residual claims, repurchases, warranties, complaints and buyer conduct shall be monitored.
POL-CR-080.14 AI boundary
The agent may prepare inventories and compare bids but shall not select buyers, determine legal transfer or approve sale.
7. Minimum Control Framework
